scope: Recorded-video server-encoded HLS short steady-state matrix and random-seek breakdown on Galaxy Chrome

conditions.transport: LAN direct to an isolated local KonomiTV
conditions.recordingFixture: Nogizaka Koujichuu local-SSD MPEG-2 TS fixture
conditions.seekMetric: video.currentTime assignment to the first requestVideoFrameCallback frame at the requested HLS time
conditions.actualFFmpegHEVCOutput: libx265 Main, yuv420p, 8-bit; the browser requested the -hevc-10bit URL but the local FFmpeg backend normalizes it to 8-bit

sample.metricDefinition: video.currentTime assignment to the first requestVideoFrameCallback frame at the requested HLS time
video.currentTime assignment to the first requestVideoFrameCallback frame at the requested HLS time

serverEvidence.patPmtExtractionAfterEncoderStart: observed within about 2-5 ms on the measured restarts
serverEvidence.hevcCommand: libx265 Main yuv420p, yadif mode=1, 60000/1001, GOP 180
serverEvidence.responseContract: getSegment awaits encoded_segment_ts_future; VideoEncodingTask completes that future only after reaching the planned boundary and a random-access frame

interpretation: The 5-second matrix is a screening result, not a long-run no-drop proof.
All 16 H.264/HEVC quality runs had zero droppedVideoFrames increase and positive audio decoded-byte growth.
Both 60p runs had one 33.367 ms mediaTime interval, so strict zero cadence gaps is not established by this screen even though droppedVideoFrames stayed at zero.

Three HEVC 30p runs had a 66.7 ms requestVideoFrameCallback delivery gap while mediaTime remained at 33.367 ms steps, so those gaps indicate callback scheduling delay rather than a missing encoded frame.
For random 1080p60 seek, buffer flush and playlist reload completed in tens of milliseconds; waiting for the first server segment response byte dominated.
The target segment locations were already present in segment_map. A new sidecar seek index cannot remove the measured encoder-and-full-segment wait.
The droppedVideoFrames values collected during seek recovery are not steady-state drop counts and include decoder reset/recovery behavior.
